mikaela: Heads-up — after landing the slab-merge allocator PR we're seeing more OOMs and a P95 tail bump on paged-attention runs. Repro on nightly with long-seq chat workloads.

samir: Ugh. Any profiler dumps? Is it compaction thrash or just higher steady-state footprint? :eyes:

mikaela: Profiler snapshot from a failing run (shortened):
```
pag_attn_block_manager::compact            28.1%  (gpu cycles)
alloc/free churn                          42.7%  (alloc calls per second)
kv-cache pin/unpin                         7.4%
kernel exec                               21.8%
other                                     0.0%
```
Compaction count jumped ~3x vs previous baseline after slab-merge. Peak GPU mem increased ~200MB on 1B-token mix.

samir: OK that points to more frequent compaction rather than a single huge leak. Two quick hypotheses: (1) smaller block_size means more fragmentation after merges, (2) our compaction threshold is too aggressive now that we merged slabs.

alex: Reproduced locally. Running quick A/B with `block_size=64k` (current) vs `block_size=128k`. Command I used: `./run_perf.sh --bench paged-attn --seq 2048 --concurrency 8 --seed 42`. Flamegraph link: https://internal/fg/1772 (private).

mikaela: Paste of the config diff I tried:
```ini
[block_manager]
block_size = 128k      # was 64k
compaction_trigger_percent = 40  # was 30
pin_hot_blocks = true  # new flag: keep recently-used blocks pinned for N requests
pin_window = 5
```

samir: Results from my canary (5 runs each):
- baseline (64k / compaction 30%): compactions/run 74, peak GPU 9.8GB, P95 latency 142ms
- 128k / compaction 40% / pin: compactions/run 21, peak GPU 10.2GB, P95 latency 118ms
- notes: overall GPU time for compaction dropped ~65%. Kernel exec unchanged.

jen: Interesting. So we trade ~400MB peak for much fewer compactions and better tail latency. How does this interact with KV cache (hot prefixes)? If we pin hot blocks we might hurt multi-tenant density.

mikaela: Good point. I ran a mixed-tenant sim with two tenants (heavy vs light): pinning reduced cross-tenant evictions by ~30% for the heavy tenant, but overall cluster-level memory utilization went up ~3%. For Dedicated it's probably fine, for Shared we should gate by customer tier.

alex: Also measured compaction CPU/GPU overlap: compactions currently run as synchronous GPU kernels and block scanning is done on CPU. There's a ~20ms window where we stall the stream while we compact. If we switch to incremental compaction (compact at sub-block granularity) we could reduce stalls but might increase kernel call overhead.

samir: Proposed next steps:
1) Roll a canary with `block_size=128k + compaction_trigger=40%` to eng-runtime pool (low qps) and monitor OOMs/latency for 24h.
2) Add telemetry: compaction_count, compaction_ms, pinned_blocks_ratio, fragmentation_ratio (free_bytes / alloc_bytes).
3) Experiment with deferred/incremental compaction: compact only when a request would otherwise OOM.

mikaela: I sketched a tiny patch to the block manager to avoid eager compaction on eviction: only kick compaction when free_space < requested_size + hysteresis. Quick diff:
```diff
- if (free_pct < threshold) compact();
+ if (free_pct < threshold && free_bytes < requested_bytes + hysteresis) compact();
```
This cut compaction invocations in my local runs by ~40% without changing block_size.

jen: Sounds safe as a first mitigation. Can we also expose `pin_hot_blocks` as an account-level feature flag? I can coordinate gating in Console.

infra-bot: deploy:eng-runtime canary/allocator-tune v2026.3.17-09:12 deployed to cluster rt-canary-2 (CI).

samir: I'll own the canary and the telemetry dashboards. Mikaela can drive the feature-flag gating for Shared vs Dedicated. Alex can prototype incremental compaction later this week.

mikaela: I'll add the flag and a doc blurb describing the cost/latency tradeoff and guidance: "Dedicated: prefer larger blocks + pin_hot_blocks; Shared: keep 64k and conservative compaction unless customer opts in."

alex: I'll upload flamegraphs and a short profile note to the perf board when the canary finishes.

jen: Great. Please post numbers back here once the 24h canary finishes. :+1:

samir: kicking it off now. will report at ~1772240400 (tomorrow).
